name: Draw over other apps
plain: Lets the app draw windows on top of other apps.
meaning: Overlays power chat heads and screen filters but are the classic tool for tapjacking and fake login screens. Android 12 limits untrusted touches through overlays.

android.prompt_ui: Settings toggle: Display over other apps
android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Display over other apps
android.store_policy: Play: allowed for core functionality; review for sensitive uses
android.note: Android 12 hides overlay windows during sensitive prompts and blocks touch pass-through above 0.8 opacity.

ios.note: iOS has no cross-app overlay; closest are Picture in Picture and Live Activities.

limits.headline: Can draw windows over other apps on Android if you flip a switch, never on iPhone
limits.user_action: You turn on Display over other apps for this app in Android settings
can: Show a floating button or bubble above other apps on Android
Show a small panel such as a chat head or screen timer
Use Picture in Picture or Live Activities on iPhone as the nearest tools
cannot: Draw over other apps on iPhone; no cross-app overlay exists
Show over sensitive prompts on Android 12 and newer, where overlays are hidden
Pass your taps through when the overlay is mostly solid (above 0.8 opacity)
Turn the switch on itself; you must do it in Settings
limits.differs: Android has this permission, off by default. iPhone has no overlay, only Picture in Picture and Live Activities.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app draw windows on top of other apps.
story.for_you: You may see a floating chat bubble, a screen filter or a recording button that sits above other apps. You have to turn this on in Settings. Bad apps can use it to cover real screens with fake ones.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for chat bubbles, screen recorders, call overlays and accessibility tools. It is also the classic tool for tapjacking, so Google limits touches through overlays.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows a floating bubble for a new message above whatever app you are using.
A game helper shows a small timer or map above a game while you play.
A blue light filter app dims the screen by drawing a tinted layer over everything.
A screen recorder shows a small stop button floating above your apps.
A driver app shows a floating button for the next ride while the driver uses maps.
Banking malware draws a fake login screen over the real bank app to steal passwords.
A tool shows large buttons above apps for people who have trouble tapping.

story.android_note: Uses the Draw over other apps setting, and Android 12 limits untrusted touches through overlays.
story.ios_note: iPhone does not allow drawing over other apps at all.

history.change: Untrusted touch blocking and hide-overlay API
Overlay type TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY replaces system alert types
